item.title: 'Total incinerated destruction': Canada wildfire evacuees wonder if they still have homes
item.description: More than 12,000 people have been forced to evacuate over the weekend after a wildfire quickly tore through Canada's picturesque Okanagan region.

item.title: 'Not afraid to stay': The Canadians who want to change how wildfires are fought
item.description: With wildfires now widespread and frequent, some rural residents in Canada are learning how to fight the flames themselves and protect their own homes.

item.title: Netanyahu's rejection of Trump's 15-point Gaza plan unlikely to be final word
item.description: The Trump administration is said to be unbothered by the Israeli prime minister's rejection of the deal, viewing it as campaign rhetoric ahead of a general election.

item.title: Taylor Farms recalls jalapeno products after salmonella outbreak
item.description: Food producer Taylor Farms is recalling sandwiches, sauces and dips across 26 US states after a salmonella outbreak.

item.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez says she's freezing her eggs
item.description: The Democratic congresswoman says she wants to "normalise" conversations about the process.

item.title: Man arrested after boat capsizes near Statue of Liberty killing woman and infant
item.description: "What was meant to be a joyful family outing ended in unimaginable tragedy," said colleagues of the woman who died.

item.title: An unbearable rotting stench is plaguing an LA neighbourhood
item.description: Heaps of rotting meat have been festering in the summer sun after a fire ripped through a huge food warehouse.

item.title: Trump's ex-lawyer Todd Blanche narrowly confirmed as US attorney general
item.description: The vote cements Trump's former criminal defence lawyer as the nation's top law enforcement official despite a rare pushback from some Republicans.

item.title: Hunter Biden tells BBC his pardon was 'not good' for US or his father's legacy
item.description: In a wide-ranging BBC interview, the former president's son denies any interest in running for office and says his father's cancer has spread.

item.title: Hormuz talks positive, Oman says, as Iran warns deal would not open strait
item.description: Both sides suggest progress in talks to agree a new shipping route through the strait, but a breakthrough remains unclear.

item.title: Residents warned to brace for the worst as Canada wildfire rages out of control
item.description: One person has died in the Bald Range wildfire in British Columbia which has spread over 53 sq miles.

item.title: Madonna pays tribute to 'genius, otherworldly' producer William Orbit
item.description: The Queen of Pop worked with Orbit several times over the years, most notably on her genre-bending, Grammy Award-winning album Ray of Light.

item.title: Coroners try to identify dozens of bodies kept in 'deplorable conditions' at US funeral home
item.description: The medical examiner's office in Chicago said the process to identify the remains could take days.

item.title: Trump administration to pay German firm $1.2bn to halt US wind projects
item.description: The RWE payout is the latest in a string of deals cancelling wind energy projects, a power source long derided by Trump.

item.title: Hunter Biden opens up to the BBC about father's cancer battle, pardon and politics
item.description: Hunter Biden talks to BBC Newsnight about his father's decision to issue him a pardon, his own political future and the former president's battle with cancer.

item.title: Watch: Pentagon releases fresh UFO videos in new document dump
item.description: The fifth batch of files released on 7 August include 41 documents, images and videos related to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP).

item.title: 'My neighbourhood is just gone' - BBC sees devastation from Washington state fires
item.description: Officials are still working to contain the blazes that have burned down at least 860 buildings.

item.title: South Korea space agency shares Moon images after SpaceX rocket debris crash
item.description: Seoul's lunar orbiter captured images of the Moon before and after part of SpaceX's rocket hit its surface on Wednesday.

item.title: Team of former prison inmates on frontline of Spokane wildfires
item.description: The Arcadia 20 team worked on preventing the spread of the Autumn Lane fire that continues to threaten areas of Spokane, Washington.

item.title: What is birthright citizenship and how common is birth tourism in the US?
item.description: The Trump administration is trying to restrict access to US citizenship for some people through attempts to end birth tourism and tighten other criteria.

item.title: Cashing in on SpaceX: 'Every chance I get, I'll sell a little more'
item.description: Andre Lavoie joined SpaceX in 2009 as an engineer, now he's looking to cash in his shares in the company.

item.title: El-Sayed's victory sends tremors through Democratic Party
item.description: His win in Michigan sets up a high-stakes contest in November, testing a left-wing candidate's popularity in a swing state.

item.title: What can scientists learn from a stray SpaceX rocket hitting the Moon?
item.description: While the collision was an accident, it is a unique scientific gift for planetary geologists that could provide important data for future space missions.

item.title: Analysis: Trump challenged by cold reality from top allies
item.description: A president used to bending US politics to his will faces two stinging losses in a matter of days, writes the BBC's Anthony Zurcher.

item.title: Did Iran hack water systems in at least seven US states?
item.description: President Donald Trump has said Iran is not to blame, but cyber experts tell the BBC it is likely the attack was directed by Tehran.
